author: New Mexico Sun
title: Lobos projected ninth in Mountain West volleyball preseason coaches' poll
text:
New Mexico has been projected to finish ninth in the Mountain West Conference volleyball preseason poll, as voted by the league’s coaches ahead of the 2025 season. The announcement was made Wednesday from Colorado Springs.
Utah State leads the preseason poll with 114 points and seven first-place votes. The Aggies are coming off a 15-14 overall record in 2024, going 12-6 in conference play under head coach Rob Neilson, and have appeared in the Mountain West tournament each year since its return in 2021.
This season marks an expansion for the Mountain West, which now includes 12 teams after Grand Canyon joined as a new member.
The full preseason rankings place Utah State at the top, followed by Colorado State with three first-place votes and San Diego State, which received two first-place votes. Fresno State is ranked fourth, Boise State fifth, with UNLV and Wyoming tied for sixth. Grand Canyon enters at eighth place. New Mexico follows at ninth, ahead of Nevada, San José State, and Air Force.
Fresno State senior Addison Haluska has been named the MW Women’s Volleyball Preseason Player of the Year. She joins Boise State’s Bre Mitchell, San Diego State’s Taylor Underwood, UNLV’s Basia Latos, Utah State’s Tierney Barlow and Kayliee Kofe, and Wyoming’s Paige Lauterwasser on this year’s preseason all-conference team.
The Lobos begin their schedule with an exhibition match against Division II New Mexico Highlands at Johnson Center on August 23. The regular season starts at home during the Lobo Invitational (August 29-30), featuring matches against Manhattan, Northern Arizona, and Houston Christian. Conference play begins with home games versus Utah State on September 25 and Boise State on September 27.
Season tickets for all 13 regular-season home matches are available through GoLobos.com/VBTickets; single-game ticket sales open August 18.
Head Coach Jon Newman-Gonchar enters his seventh season aiming to guide New Mexico back to the Mountain West Tournament after missing out last year. In 2024, New Mexico finished ninth in conference standings with a 13-15 overall record (6-12 MW). Despite a midseason nine-match losing streak, they closed strong by winning four of their last six games. The team led the conference in digs per set (15.77) for a third consecutive year and ranked second in blocks per set (2.53).
The program faces roster changes after graduating four starters but returns eight players who contributed last season. Additionally, two freshmen and four transfers—two from other Division I programs—have joined the squad.
Under Newman-Gonchar over the past four seasons, New Mexico has posted a .585 win percentage and gone 33-18 at home. Attendance averaged over 800 fans per game last year for a third straight season; a high of 1,387 fans attended their matchup against New Mexico State on September 16.
Fans can attend next Saturday's exhibition match against New Mexico Highlands free of charge at Johnson Center starting at 1:30 p.m., with opportunities to meet players afterward. The event will not be streamed but live statistics will be available via GoLobos.com/VBStats.
After that exhibition match, New Mexico hosts Manhattan, Northern Arizona and Houston Christian as part of the Lobo Invitational (August 30–31). A tournament pass is available that covers all three home matches for the price of two through GoLobos.com/VBTickets when single-game tickets go live August 18.
For updates throughout the season—including coverage and promotional information—fans can follow @UNMLoboVB on social media platforms.
